name: The tongue taste map is a myth

hook_variants.template: The taste map you saw in school is a lie.
Are bitter taste buds really only at the back of your tongue?
That tongue diagram from biology class? Totally wrong.

sections.text: The 'sweet at the tip, bitter at the back' tongue map was debunked decades ago.
Every taste bud can sense all five basic tastes. They're spread across your whole tongue.
sections.title: reality

sections.text: The myth came from a mistranslated 1901 German study.
sections.title: the myth

sections.text: You have roughly 2,000 to 10,000 taste buds, replaced every week or two.
sections.subtitle: taste buds, refreshed ~every 2 weeks

sections.text: So your tongue is one big equal-opportunity sensor. School was wrong.
Follow for more myths crushed by science.

facts.claim: The tongue map showing distinct regions for sweet, sour, salty and bitter is a common misconception and false
The myth originated from a mistranslation of a 1901 German paper by David Hänig
Humans have between 2,000 and 10,000 taste buds that are replaced every one to two weeks
